stem: Point A has coordinates N 120.00, E 340.00 and point B has coordinates N 300.00, E 460.00, in metres. What is the azimuth of the line from A to B?
eli5: The direction between two coordinated points comes from the differences in easting and northing: tan(azimuth) = change in easting / change in northing. The signs of the two differences fix the quadrant, so add 180° or 360° to the calculator result when the line does not run north-east.
solution:
Change in northing = 300.00 - 120.00 = 180.00 m. Change in easting = 460.00 - 340.00 = 120.00 m. Both are positive, so the line runs north-east.

Azimuth = arctan(\frac{120.00}{180.00}) = 33.69°.

Length = \sqrt{180.00^{2} + 120.00^{2}} = 216.33 m.
